messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Synthetic canary heartbeat missing in eu-west-1 for 3 consecutive intervals. Probe group=canary-eu-heartbeat, failures=3/3, 95th latency spike. Auto-page triggered.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-INC-48291 created -> https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-INC-48291 (severity: high). Escalation policy: canary-synth. Acknowledgement required.

lee.sre: acked in PD. I’m on call. Quick check: is this probe failure or origin backend 5xx?

incident-bot: Probe logs show 502 from prober-runner in eu-west-1, collector errors: "upstream reset by peer" and transient 429s from probe-aggregator.

maya.support: seeing two customer reports about slow tokenization in eu users (support-tickets #3389, #3392). Not widespread yet but likely correlated.

lee.sre: ok opening the prober console, pulling last 15m.

taylor.sre: I’m with lee — i’m seeing probe fanout dropped to 0.6x and connection retries to aggregator increasing. Could be rate-limit or a mistaken config rollout. Did we deploy any prober changes to eu yesterday?

anil.eng: rolled a small config at 02:10 UTC yesterday to reduce prober timeout (PR #5421). I reverted locally once we noticed some noise in canary but didn’t push revert to prod.

lee.sre: copy. Let’s mitigations: 1) disable fanout spike aggressor, 2) increase prober timeout back to 5s, 3) restart prober pod group in eu-west-1. I’ll run commands.

lee.sre: running:```bash
kubectl -n proberrollouts set env deployment/canary-prober PROBE_TIMEOUT=5000 --record
kubectl -n proberrollouts rollout restart deployment/canary-prober -l region=eu-west-1
```

incident-bot: Action recorded: PROBE_TIMEOUT change. Restart initiated.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-48291 acknowledged by lee.sre. Current assignees: lee.sre.

julia-oncall: FYI i'm switching on-call duties in 20m; if this escalates please loop me in.

taylor.sre: after restart prober pods come up but we still see 2/3 failed intervals for one test runner. Logs show aggregator returning 429 with header 'X-RateLimit-Reset' present. Looks like downstream throttling.

anil.eng: aggregators autoscale threshold got hit, but we have burst capacity. Can someone toggle temporary bypass for canary traffic to a different ingress?

lee.sre: routing knob available: canary routing -> route-to: fallback-collector-eu. Doing switch now:```json
{"route_override":"fallback-collector-eu","reason":"mitigation for PD-INC-48291"}
```

incident-bot: Route override applied. Canary traffic routed to fallback-collector-eu.

taylor.sre: immediate improvement: probe failures drop to 0/3 and 95th latency normalizing. Looks like original collector was rate-limiting canary fanout.

maya.support: customer reports show degraded responses stopped around 02:48 UTC, matching this mitigation. I’ll update the two tickets.

lee.sre: closing immediate impact: restored. Remaining actions: follow-up RCA, update probe rollout gating, add jitter and backoff to prober fanout, and add a PD suppression rule for planned canary rollouts.

anil.eng: noted — i’ll add jitter+backoff default and create PR for rollout gating (link in thread when ready).

julia-oncall: taking handoff now — thanks lee. I’ll own the follow-up next 24h.

lee.sre: handing off to julia-oncall — summary: PD-INC-48291 triggered by aggregator rate-limit causing synthetic canary heartbeat misses in eu-west-1. Mitigation: revert aggressive prober timeout, route canary to fallback collector, restarted prober pods. Customer impact limited to a few EU customers with slow tokenization.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-48291 status changed to Resolved by lee.sre at 6823461199. Resolution note: routing override + pod restart mitigated failures.

maya.support: updated customer tickets and added post-incident note.

lee.sre: quick postmortem todo: short RCA draft, add runbook steps for collector-backpressure (include how to apply route override), and add automated alert to break out aggregator rate-limit spikes. Assigning to anil.eng for code change, taylor.sre for runbook.

anil.eng: will open PR and schedule canary to test jitter in staging.

messages: end of thread.
